examples.ko: 내일 아침 여섯 시에 모닝콜 부탁드려요.
examples.en: Please give me a wake-up call at six tomorrow morning.
I got a wake-up call at the hotel and barely got up.

examples.ko: 알람이 안 들려서 친구한테 모닝콜을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't hear my alarm, so I asked a friend for a wake-up call.

examples.ko: 모닝콜이 울려도 저는 또 잠들어 버렸어요.
examples.en: Even when the wake-up call rang, I fell asleep again.
Is the wake-up call service free at this hotel?

examples.ko: 남편이 매일 아침 일곱 시에 모닝콜을 해 줘요.
examples.en: My husband gives me a wake-up call every morning at seven.

explain: 호텔에서는 '모닝콜 서비스'라고 많이 말해요. 친구나 가족이 전화로 깨워 줄 때도 '모닝콜 해 줘'라고 말해요. 휴대폰에서 울리는 소리는 보통 '알람'이라고 해요.
explain_en: At hotels you often hear '모닝콜 서비스'. When a friend or family member phones to wake you, you can say '모닝콜 해 줘'. The sound your phone makes is usually called '알람'.

examples.en: The bathwater temperature is just right.

examples.ko: 목욕물이 너무 뜨거워서 찬물을 조금 섞었어요.
examples.en: The bathwater was too hot, so I mixed in a little cold water.

examples.ko: 아이를 위해 따뜻한 목욕물을 받아 놓았어요.
examples.en: I ran some warm bathwater for the child.
I put a little salt in the bathwater and I feel refreshed.
Get in quickly before the bathwater cools down.
I forgot to drain the bathwater from the tub.

explain: 목욕물은 '받다'와 잘 어울려서 '목욕물을 받다'라고 말해요. 물을 뺄 때는 '빼다'를 써요. '목욕물 온도'처럼 온도를 말할 때도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It pairs naturally with '받다', so you say '목욕물을 받다' for running a bath. To drain it, use '빼다'. It also often appears in phrases about temperature, like '목욕물 온도'.

examples.en: My bag got heavy because it got soaked in the rain.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 몸이 무거워지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like my body gets heavier as I get older.
The luggage got heavier and heavier, so I rested for a moment.
I'm sleepy, so my eyelids keep getting heavy.
My heart grew heavy after hearing that story.

examples.ko: 가방이 무거워질까 봐 책은 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: I left the books behind in case the bag got too heavy.

explain: '무겁다'는 ㅂ불규칙이라 '무거워요'가 되고, 여기에 '-지다'가 붙어서 '무거워져요'가 돼요. 물건뿐 아니라 몸, 눈꺼풀, 마음, 분위기에도 쓸 수 있어요. 반대말은 '가벼워지다'예요.
explain_en: '무겁다' is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so it becomes '무거워요', and adding '-지다' gives '무거워져요'. It works for objects but also for the body, eyelids, feelings and atmosphere. The opposite is '가벼워지다'.

examples.en: Someone is waiting outside the door.
It's cold, so I don't want to go outside.
The child ran out through the door.

examples.ko: 문밖의 소리가 시끄러워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The noise outside the door was loud, so I couldn't sleep.
Please leave the package outside the door.
It had snowed, so everything outside the door was white.

explain: 문 바로 바깥쪽을 말할 때 써요. 집 전체의 바깥은 '집 밖'이나 '바깥'이라고 해요. 보통 '문밖에', '문밖으로'처럼 조사를 붙여서 위치나 방향을 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the area right outside a door. For the outside of a whole house, people say '집 밖' or '바깥'. It usually takes particles, as in '문밖에' or '문밖으로', to show location or direction.

examples.ko: 이 정도 비는 우산 없이도 문제없어요.
examples.en: Rain this light is no problem even without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 제가 도와 드릴 테니까 문제없을 거예요.
examples.en: I'll help you, so it won't be a problem.
If the schedule works, I'll start next week.

examples.ko: 검사 결과는 모두 문제없는 것으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The test results all came out fine.
As long as you keep to the appointment time, it's fine.
Is it okay to play games on this computer?

explain: '문제가 없다'와 같은 뜻인데, 붙여서 한 단어로 써요. '괜찮아요'보다 기능이나 조건, 상태에 이상이 없다고 확인해 주는 느낌이에요. 상대가 걱정할 때 '네, 문제없어요'라고 짧게 대답하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '문제가 없다' but is written as one word. Compared with '괜찮아요', it feels more like confirming that a function, condition or state has no issue. You can also answer a worried person briefly with '네, 문제없어요'.

examples.ko: 이 노트북은 영상 편집도 문제없이 돼요.
examples.en: This laptop can handle video editing without any problem.
The exam ended without any problems.
The service runs smoothly even when the number of users grows.
The plane arrived on time without any trouble.

examples.ko: 그 일은 저 혼자서도 문제없이 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can do that job on my own without any trouble.
The app installed on my phone without any problem.

explain: '문제없이 되다', '문제없이 돌아가다', '문제없이 끝나다'처럼 일이 막힘없이 진행될 때 써요. '무사히'는 위험한 일을 지나서 안전하게라는 느낌이 강하고, '문제없이'는 오류나 불편이 없다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when things proceed smoothly, as in '문제없이 되다', '문제없이 돌아가다' or '문제없이 끝나다'. '무사히' leans toward getting through something risky safely, while '문제없이' means no errors or trouble.

en: playing in the water; water play

examples.en: In summer I go play in the water with my family.

examples.ko: 수영장에서 물놀이를 하기 전에 준비 운동을 해요.
examples.en: I warm up before playing in the water at the pool.
The weather is great for playing in the water today.
It rained, so we couldn't play in the water.
Be sure to bring a tube when you go play in the water.
After playing in the water, I take a shower with warm water.

explain: 수영처럼 실력을 보여 주는 운동이 아니라 계곡, 바다, 수영장에서 물에 들어가 노는 것을 말해요. '물놀이를 하다/가다'로 많이 써요. '사물놀이'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Unlike swimming as exercise, it is about getting into water at a valley, beach or pool just to play. It is often used as '물놀이를 하다/가다'. It sounds a bit like '사물놀이', but that is a completely different word.

examples.en: One plate of boiled dumplings, please.
In winter I crave warm boiled dumplings.
I ordered boiled dumplings instead of fried ones.
Boiled dumplings taste good dipped in soy sauce.

examples.ko: 이 집은 물만두 속이 정말 꽉 차 있어요.
examples.en: The filling in this place's boiled dumplings is really packed.

examples.ko: 엄마가 집에서 직접 빚은 물만두를 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mom gave me boiled dumplings she made at home.

explain: 메뉴판에서는 기름에 구운 '군만두', 찐 '찐만두'와 나란히 나올 때가 많아요. 만둣국과 달리 보통 국물에 말지 않고 건져서 간장에 찍어 먹어요.
explain_en: On menus it often appears next to '군만두' (pan-fried) and '찐만두' (steamed). Unlike '만둣국', it is usually not served in soup but lifted out and dipped in soy sauce.

examples.en: I always wear goggles when I swim.
My goggles fogged up.

examples.ko: 우리 아이 물안경 좀 골라 주세요.
examples.en: Please help me pick out goggles for my child.
Opening your eyes without goggles stings.
My goggles have blue lenses.
The goggle strap is too tight.

explain: 수영장에서는 '수경'이라고도 말해요. 얼굴에 착용할 때는 '쓰다'와 '끼다'를 둘 다 쓸 수 있어요. 눈을 보호하려고 쓰는 거라 '물안경 없이 수영하다'처럼도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: At pools people also call it '수경'. For wearing it, both '쓰다' and '끼다' work. Since it protects your eyes, you also often hear things like '물안경 없이 수영하다'.

examples.en: I filled the water glass to the brim.
I broke a glass and cut my hand a little.

examples.ko: 아침 물 한 잔을 위해 머리맡에 물컵을 올려 뒀어요.
examples.en: For my morning glass of water, I put a cup by my bed.
This glass is made of glass, so you have to be careful.
Please bring two water glasses.
When I do the dishes, I wash the water glasses first.

explain: '컵'은 종이컵, 머그컵처럼 종류가 많아서 물 마시는 용도를 분명히 할 때 '물컵'이라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '물잔'도 있어요. 물은 '따르다'와 함께 써서 '물컵에 물을 따르다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '컵' covers many kinds, such as paper cups and mugs, so '물컵' makes clear it is for drinking water. '물잔' is a similar word. It goes with '따르다', as in '물컵에 물을 따르다'.

examples.en: The child came down the slide happily.
I tried to climb up the slide but kept slipping.
The playground has swings and a slide.
My younger sibling came down the slide upside down.

examples.ko: 미끄럼틀은 한 명씩 차례대로 타야 해요.
examples.en: You have to take turns going down the slide one at a time.
My child runs over whenever she sees a slide.

explain: '미끄럼틀을 타다'가 짝이 되는 표현이에요. '미끄럽다', '미끄러지다'와 소리와 뜻이 가까워서 같이 기억하면 쉬워요. 놀이터에서 그네, 시소와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The natural collocation is '미끄럼틀을 타다'. Its sound and meaning are close to '미끄럽다' and '미끄러지다', so learning them together helps. It often appears with swings and seesaws at playgrounds.

examples.ko: 해가 지면 바닷바람 때문에 훨씬 추워져요.
examples.en: After sunset it gets much colder because of the sea breeze.
The sea breeze is cool and it makes me feel good.
I walked along the beach in the sea breeze.

examples.ko: 해안 마을은 바닷바람 덕분에 빨래가 빨리 말라요.
examples.en: Thanks to the sea breeze, laundry dries fast in coastal towns.
The sea breeze made a mess of my hair.
The sea breeze has a slightly salty smell.

explain: '바람을 맞다'처럼 '바닷바람을 맞다'라고 많이 말해요. 비슷하게 '산바람', '강바람'도 있어요. 조금 딱딱하게 말하면 '해풍'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: People often say '바닷바람을 맞다', like '바람을 맞다'. Similar words include '산바람' and '강바람'. In a more formal register, it is also called '해풍'.

examples.en: I was so glad to see my friend after a long time.
In my delight, I shouted without realizing it.
He couldn't hide his delight and smiled.
I felt surprise before I felt gladness.
I was half glad and half worried.

examples.ko: 오래된 편지를 읽고 반가움과 그리움을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: Reading the old letter, I felt gladness and longing.

explain: '반갑다'에서 나온 말로, 만나거나 소식을 들었을 때의 기쁜 마음을 말해요. 그냥 '기쁨'보다 사람이나 소식과 연결된 느낌이에요. 직접 인사할 때는 명사보다 '반가워요'를 써요.
explain_en: It comes from '반갑다' and describes the happy feeling on meeting someone or hearing news. Compared with plain '기쁨', it is tied to a person or news. When greeting someone directly, say '반가워요' rather than this noun.

examples.en: It was hot, so I wore a short-sleeved T-shirt.
It's still a bit chilly for short sleeves.
Even in winter I stay in short sleeves at home.
Not the short-sleeved shirt, please give me the long-sleeved one.
The neck of this short-sleeved shirt is stretched out.

examples.ko: 안에 반소매를 입고 위에 카디건을 걸쳤어요.
examples.en: I wore a short-sleeved shirt and put a cardigan over it.

explain: 반대말은 '긴소매'예요. 일상에서는 '반팔'이라고도 많이 말해요. 옷은 '입다'와 함께 써서 '반소매를 입다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '긴소매'. In everyday talk people also say '반팔'. It goes with '입다', as in '반소매를 입다'.

examples.en: I hear footsteps from upstairs late at night.
The child tiptoed along, muffling the sound of his steps.
I can tell it's Dad just from the footsteps.

examples.ko: 누가 오는지 발소리로 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can tell who is coming by the footsteps.
The footsteps woke me up.
The upstairs neighbor's footsteps sound really loud.

explain: '발소리가 나다/들리다', '발소리를 죽이다'처럼 자주 써요. '발자국 소리'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, '발자국'만 말하면 땅에 남은 자국이에요. 아파트에서는 층간 소음 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Common patterns are '발소리가 나다/들리다' and '발소리를 죽이다'. '발자국 소리' means the same, but '발자국' alone is the mark left on the ground. It often comes up in talk about noise between apartment floors.

examples.en: There's a good little restaurant near my office.
For lunch I eat a set meal at a neighborhood restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 밥집은 반찬이 정말 많이 나와요.
examples.en: This restaurant serves a lot of side dishes.

examples.ko: 퇴근하고 혼자 밥집에 들러서 저녁을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After work I stopped by a small restaurant and had dinner alone.
The lady at the restaurant gave me more side dishes.

examples.ko: 이 근처에 괜찮은 밥집 좀 알아요?
examples.en: Do you know any decent place to eat around here?

explain: '식당'보다 가볍고 친근한 말로, 밥과 찌개, 반찬을 파는 작은 가게 느낌이에요. 커피를 파는 '카페'나 술을 파는 '술집'과 대비해서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a lighter, friendlier word than '식당', suggesting a small place serving rice, stew and side dishes. It is also used in contrast with '카페' for coffee or '술집' for drinks.

examples.ko: 이번 달 방세를 아직 못 냈어요.
examples.en: I haven't paid this month's rent yet.
The rent went up too much, so I'm planning to move.
I pay the rent on the last day of every month.
Is the maintenance fee included in the rent?
I'm very worried about the rent.
The rent is three months overdue.

explain: 집 전체보다 방 하나를 빌릴 때 느낌이 강해요. 집 전체에 대한 월 임대료는 '월세'나 '집세'라고 해요. '방세를 내다', '방세가 밀리다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It feels more like renting a single room than a whole home. For monthly rent on a whole place, people say '월세' or '집세'. Common patterns are '방세를 내다' and '방세가 밀리다'.

examples.en: My family makes napa cabbage kimchi ourselves.
Just rice and cabbage kimchi is delicious.
I made kimchi stew with well-fermented cabbage kimchi.

examples.ko: 배추김치는 보통 겨울 전에 많이 담가요.
examples.en: People usually make a lot of cabbage kimchi before winter.

examples.ko: 배추김치 한 포기를 통째로 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought one whole head of cabbage kimchi.
I learned about the seasoning that goes into cabbage kimchi.

explain: 그냥 '김치'라고 하면 보통 배추김치를 떠올려요. 무로 만든 '깍두기'나 '총각김치'와 구별하고 싶을 때 '배추김치'라고 말해요. 김치 재료를 말할 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: When people just say '김치', they usually mean cabbage kimchi. '배추김치' is used when you want to distinguish it from radish kimchi such as '깍두기' or '총각김치'. It is natural when talking about kimchi ingredients.

examples.en: I took in a puppy that had been abandoned on the street.
Trash is being dumped carelessly into the sea.

examples.ko: 창고에 버려져 있던 의자를 고쳐 썼어요.
examples.en: I fixed up a chair that had been left discarded in the storeroom.

examples.ko: 아직 먹을 수 있는 음식이 많이 버려져요.
examples.en: A lot of food that is still edible gets thrown away.
He felt that he had been abandoned by his family.

examples.ko: 버려지는 옷이 줄도록 중고 가게를 이용해요.
examples.en: I use secondhand shops so that less clothing gets thrown away.

explain: '버리다'의 피동 표현이에요. '누가 버렸다'보다 버려진 결과나 상태에 초점이 있어서 '버려져 있다'로 자주 써요. 사람이나 동물에게 쓰면 안타까운 느낌이 커요.
explain_en: This is the passive form of '버리다'. It focuses on the result or state of being discarded rather than who did it, so '버려져 있다' is common. Used for people or animals, it carries a sad feeling.

examples.en: I'm learning Vietnamese.
Please teach me how to greet someone in Vietnamese.
My friend is good at both Korean and Vietnamese.
Vietnamese has tones, so it's difficult.
This menu also has Vietnamese descriptions.
We are looking for a Vietnamese interpreter.

explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 '-어'를 붙이면 그 나라 언어가 돼요. 한국어, 일본어, 중국어처럼요. '베트남 말'이라고 풀어서 말할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: Adding '-어' after a country name gives its language, as in 한국어, 일본어 and 중국어. You can also say it more loosely as '베트남 말'.

en: be taken ill; catch a disease

examples.en: I overworked myself and fell ill.
She is a frail child, so she often gets sick.
What should we do if someone gets sick during the trip?
Get plenty of rest before you get sick.
I'm worried so much that I think I'll get sick.

examples.ko: 그 일로 병난 사람이 한둘이 아니에요.
examples.en: Quite a few people got sick because of that.

explain: '병이 나다'를 붙여 쓴 말이에요. 그냥 '아프다'보다 무리하거나 걱정해서 몸이 상했다는 느낌이 강해요. '몸살이 나다', '탈이 나다'와 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is '병이 나다' written as one word. Compared with plain '아프다', it more strongly suggests that overwork or worry has worn the body down. It is used much like '몸살이 나다' or '탈이 나다'.

examples.en: I had barley rice bibimbap for lunch.

examples.ko: 보리밥에 나물을 넣고 고추장으로 비벼 먹어요.
examples.en: I put namul on the barley rice and mix it with gochujang.
This restaurant is famous for its tasty barley rice.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할머니가 보리밥을 자주 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my grandmother often made barley rice for me.
Barley rice has more chewiness than plain white rice.
For my health, I switched to barley rice.

explain: 쌀로만 지은 '쌀밥', 여러 곡식을 섞은 '잡곡밥'과 구별해서 말해요. 식당에서는 '보리밥 정식'이나 '보리밥집'처럼 나물과 함께 나오는 메뉴로 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It is distinguished from '쌀밥' (rice only) and '잡곡밥' (mixed grains). At restaurants you often see it as a set meal served with namul, such as '보리밥 정식' or at a '보리밥집'.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the bowling alley with friends.
I rented shoes at the bowling alley.

examples.ko: 이 볼링장은 레인이 스무 개나 돼요.
examples.en: This bowling alley has as many as twenty lanes.
A new bowling alley opened near my house.
It takes about ten minutes to walk to the bowling alley.

examples.ko: 볼링장 안은 소리가 커서 말이 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: It's loud inside the bowling alley, so it's hard to hear each other.

explain: '-장'은 장소를 나타내서 수영장, 주차장, 운동장처럼 써요. 볼링은 '치다'와 함께 써서 '볼링을 치다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-장' marks a place, as in 수영장, 주차장 and 운동장. Bowling goes with '치다', so you say '볼링을 치다'.

examples.en: This weekend I'm going on a spring outing with my family.

examples.ko: 벚꽃이 피어서 봄나들이 나온 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: The cherry blossoms are out, so many people are on spring outings.
The weather today is perfect for a spring outing.
Where should we go for our spring outing this year?
During spring outing season the highways get very congested.
I set out with the kids on a spring outing to the park.

explain: '나들이'는 가까운 곳에 놀러 다녀오는 것이라서 '봄나들이를 가다/나가다/떠나다'로 써요. 학교나 단체에서 가는 '소풍'보다 가족, 친구와 가볍게 나가는 느낌이에요. '꽃구경'과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '나들이' is a short trip somewhere nearby, so you say '봄나들이를 가다/나가다/떠나다'. It feels more like a casual trip with family or friends than a school or group '소풍'. It often appears alongside '꽃구경'.

examples.ko: 봄이 오면 맛있는 봄나물을 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: When spring comes, you can eat delicious spring greens.
I bought a bag of spring greens at the market.
I made bibimbap with spring greens.
Spring greens are blanched and then seasoned by hand.

examples.ko: 봄나물에는 비타민이 많아서 피로 회복에 좋아요.
examples.en: Spring greens are rich in vitamins and good for recovering from fatigue.
This restaurant's spring greens set meal is popular.

explain: 냉이, 달래, 쑥처럼 봄에 먹는 나물을 묶어서 부르는 말이에요. 산이나 들에서 '캐다'라고 하고, 먹을 때는 '무치다'를 많이 써요. 봄에는 식당 메뉴판에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a collective name for greens eaten in spring, such as 냉이, 달래 and 쑥. You '캐다' them in hills or fields, and '무치다' is the common verb for seasoning them. They often show up on restaurant menus in spring.

examples.en: The weather warmed up, so I took out my spring clothes.
I needed new spring clothes, so I went shopping.
It's still chilly, so I get cold in just spring clothes.

examples.ko: 겨울옷은 넣고 봄옷은 옷장 앞쪽에 걸었어요.
examples.en: I put away winter clothes and hung spring clothes at the front of the closet.

examples.ko: 봄옷 세일을 해서 두 벌 샀어요.
examples.en: There was a spring clothes sale, so I bought two pieces.
I changed into spring clothes and my body feels light.

explain: 계절 이름 뒤에 '옷'을 붙여 여름옷, 가을옷, 겨울옷처럼 말해요. 환절기에는 옷장을 정리하면서 '봄옷을 꺼내다', '겨울옷을 넣다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Adding '옷' after a season name gives words like 여름옷, 가을옷 and 겨울옷. When the seasons change and you tidy the closet, you often say '봄옷을 꺼내다' or '겨울옷을 넣다'.

examples.en: I'm the vice class president of our class.
The vice class president ran the meeting in place of the class president.
We elected the vice class president by vote.
The vice class president helps the class president collect homework.
My friend was chosen as vice class president and is happy.
I'm thinking of running in the vice class president election.

explain: 학교 한 반에서 '반장'을 돕는 학생이에요. '부-'는 '부회장', '부사장'처럼 한 단계 아래 직책 앞에 붙어요. 반장이 없을 때 회의를 대신 이끌기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the student who assists the '반장' in a school class. The prefix '부-' goes before ranks one step below, as in '부회장' and '부사장'. When the '반장' is absent, the '부반장' may lead the class meeting instead.

examples.en: Rain clouds are rolling in from the west.
The sky is dark because of the rain clouds.
The rain clouds will pass tomorrow afternoon.
I gazed at the rain clouds outside the window for a while.
The mountaintop is hidden by rain clouds and can't be seen.
The wind is blowing hard along with the rain clouds.

explain: '먹구름'은 검게 보이는 구름이고, '비구름'은 비를 내리는 구름이라는 점이 달라요. '비구름이 몰려오다', '비구름이 걷히다'로 자주 써요. 일기예보에서도 많이 들어요.
explain_en: '먹구름' is a dark-looking cloud, while '비구름' is a cloud that brings rain. Common patterns are '비구름이 몰려오다' and '비구름이 걷히다'. You also hear it often in weather forecasts.

examples.en: Please put the fruit in a plastic bag.

examples.ko: 비닐봉지 값을 따로 받은 뒤로 장바구니를 들고 오는 손님이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since they started charging for plastic bags, more customers bring shopping bags.
The plastic bag tore and the things spilled out.

examples.ko: 일회용 비닐봉지는 돈을 내고 사야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay for single-use plastic bags.
Could you give me one more plastic bag?
I took a shopping bag instead of a plastic bag.

explain: 줄여서 그냥 '봉지'나 '비닐'이라고도 말해요. 종이로 만든 '종이봉투'와 짝으로 생각하면 편해요. 마트에서 '봉지 필요하세요?'라고 자주 물어봐요.
explain_en: People often shorten it to just '봉지' or '비닐'. It helps to think of it as the counterpart of '종이봉투' (paper bag). At supermarkets you often hear '봉지 필요하세요?'.

examples.ko: 이 집에는 빈방이 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: This house has two empty rooms.
I lent the empty room to a friend.
If you have a vacant room, I'd like to stay just one night.
A strange noise came from the empty room.
I'm using the spare room as storage for now.

examples.ko: 빈방 하나 보여 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you show me one of the vacant rooms?

explain: '비다'의 관형형 '빈'과 '방'이 붙은 말이에요. 숙소에서는 '남는 방'이라고도 하고, 집이나 건물이 비어 있는 상태는 '공실'이라고 해요. 사람이 없는 방도, 물건 없이 쓰지 않는 방도 모두 '빈방'이에요.
explain_en: It joins '빈', the modifier form of '비다', with '방'. At lodgings people also say '남는 방', and a vacant property is called '공실'. A room with nobody in it, or a spare room that isn't used, can both be '빈방'.

en: sound of rain; sound of raindrops

examples.en: I like rain, so I like the sound of it.

examples.ko: 한옥 카페의 툇마루에서 차를 마시며 빗소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: I listened to the rain while drinking tea on the porch of a hanok cafe.
The sound of the rain kept me from sleeping well all night.
The sound of rain outside the window woke me up.
The sound of rain makes my mind feel at ease.
The smell of coffee spread along with the sound of rain.

explain: '비'와 '소리' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가서 '빗소리'로 쓰고 [비쏘리]로 읽어요. '빗소리를 듣다', '빗소리가 들리다'로 많이 써요. 비가 오는 날의 분위기를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: An 사이시옷 sits between '비' and '소리', so it is written '빗소리' and read [비쏘리]. Common patterns are '빗소리를 듣다' and '빗소리가 들리다'. It often comes up when describing the mood of a rainy day.

examples.en: I pinned the wet socks up with clothespins.
I didn't have enough clothespins, so I bought more.

examples.ko: 이불을 널 때는 빨래집게를 여러 개 써요.
examples.en: I use several clothespins when hanging out a blanket.
Clothespins are sold cheaply at housewares stores.
One of the clothespins broke.
I hang socks in a row on the clothespins to dry.

explain: '빨래'에 물건을 집는 도구 '집게'가 붙은 말이에요. 빨래는 '널다', '걷다'와 같이 쓰고, 널 때 '빨래집게로 집다'라고 해요. 빨래를 걸어 두는 건조대와는 달라요.
explain_en: It combines '빨래' (laundry) with '집게', a gripping tool. Laundry goes with '널다' (hang out) and '걷다' (take in), and you '빨래집게로 집다' to pin it. It is different from a drying rack.

examples.en: I sincerely apologize for being late.
I'd like to apologize for the inconvenience.
I'll go in person and apologize.
I think I should apologize first.

examples.ko: 고객님께 사과드렸지만 아직 화가 안 풀리셨어요.
examples.en: I apologized to the customer, but they are still upset.
I'm calling to apologize on their behalf.

explain: '사과하다'의 높임 표현이에요. 받는 사람을 높여서 윗사람이나 손님에게 사과할 때 써요. 친구에게는 '사과할게'나 '미안해'라고 해요. '사과'는 과일 apple과 소리가 같아서 문맥으로 구별해요.
explain_en: This is the honorific version of '사과하다', used to show respect to the person you apologize to, such as a superior or a customer. To a friend you'd say '사과할게' or '미안해'. '사과' also means 'apple', so context tells them apart.

examples.ko: 시험 볼 때는 컴퓨터용 사인펜을 써요.
examples.en: For exams we use a computer-readable marker pen.
I colored the drawing with a felt-tip pen.
The felt-tip pen dried out and won't write.
Felt-tip pens bleed, so be careful when you use them.
I bought a set of felt-tip pens at the stationery store.
I put one felt-tip pen in my bag.

explain: 영어로는 보통 felt-tip pen이라고 해요. '펜'은 볼펜, 만년필까지 넓게 가리키지만 '사인펜'은 끝이 부드러운 펜이에요. 세는 말은 '자루'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: In English it is usually called a felt-tip pen. '펜' covers ballpoints and fountain pens too, but '사인펜' is the soft-tipped kind. The counter word is often '자루'.

examples.en: My mother remarried, so I got a stepfather.
My stepfather treats me like his own son.
I go fishing with my stepfather.
Today is the day I greet my stepfather for the first time.
I decided to call my stepfather 'Dad'.
My stepfather's job is a chef.

explain: '새아빠'보다 조금 정중하게 말할 때 써요. 법이나 서류에서는 '계부'라고 해요. 짝이 되는 말은 '새어머니'예요.
explain_en: It sounds a little more polite than '새아빠'. In legal or official documents the term is '계부'. Its counterpart is '새어머니'.

examples.en: My stepdad plays with me every weekend.
I cooked together with my stepdad.
Mom and my stepdad got married last year.
Thanks to my stepdad, I got a new family.
I got allowance money from my stepdad.
My stepdad made a delicious dinner for me.

explain: '새아버지'보다 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '새엄마'예요. 서류에서는 '계부'라고 하고, 직접 부를 때는 보통 '아빠'나 '아버지'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a more casual spoken word than '새아버지'. Its counterpart is '새엄마'. On documents the term is '계부', and when addressing him directly people usually say '아빠' or '아버지'.

examples.en: Two fried shrimp, please.
I dipped the fried shrimp in sauce and ate it.
Fried shrimp tastes best when it's crispy.
The fried shrimp cooled down and got soggy.
The fried shrimp rice bowl is the tastiest.
Shall we have fried shrimp for dinner tonight?

explain: 튀김은 '야채튀김', '오징어튀김'처럼 재료 이름 뒤에 붙여요. 분식집에서 '튀김'을 주문하면 이런 종류가 나와요. 맛을 말할 때는 '바삭하다'가 가장 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '튀김' is attached after the ingredient, as in '야채튀김' and '오징어튀김'. At a snack shop, ordering '튀김' gets you assorted items like these. To describe its taste, '바삭하다' (crispy) fits best.

examples.ko: 봄이 되자 나무에 새잎이 나기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When spring came, new leaves started to grow on the tree.
The color of the new leaves is really pale.
One new leaf has come out on the plant in the pot.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤에 새잎은 더 푸르러졌어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the new leaves turned greener.
Seeing the new leaves puts me in a good mood.
Morning dew has formed on the new leaves.

explain: '새잎이 나다', '새잎이 돋다'처럼 써요. 화분 식물을 키울 때도 '새잎이 났어요'라고 자주 말해요. 떨어진 잎은 '낙엽'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it as '새잎이 나다' or '새잎이 돋다'. When growing houseplants, people often say '새잎이 났어요'. Leaves that have fallen are '낙엽'.

examples.en: I folded paper cranes out of colored paper.
I cut the colored paper into circles and made a card.
Could you lend me one sheet of colored paper?
Colored paper is sold at stationery stores.
The glue smeared on the colored paper and made it messy.
I need colored paper for art class today.

explain: '색종이를 접다', '색종이를 오리다', '색종이를 붙이다'처럼 손으로 만드는 활동과 같이 나와요. 크고 두꺼운 그림용 종이인 '도화지'와는 달라요. 종이접기를 할 때 특히 많이 써요.
explain_en: It appears with hands-on activities, as in '색종이를 접다' (fold), '색종이를 오리다' (cut out) and '색종이를 붙이다' (stick). It differs from '도화지', the larger, thicker drawing paper. It is especially common for origami.
